newsitem.title: USA: Florida transit chief optimistic on bullet train.
newsitem.headline: Florida transit chief optimistic on bullet train.

text.p: Florida Transportation Secretary Ben Watts said Tuesday he was optimistic about the chances of obtaining federal bond guarantees and other backing for the state's $5 billion high-speed rail project.
The state must decide by Oct 30 whether to proceed with the 320-mile rail system linking Miami, Orlando and Tampa with trains traveling 125 to 200 mph.
Watts said the discussed the project with U.S. Transportation Secretary Federico Pena during a Florida visit last week and that Pena was "supportive."
"We're still alive and we're still optimistic," Watts said.
Florida has pledged up to $70 million a year for 30 years toward the project, and has chosen an Orlando constorium to build it. But the project cannot survive without federal help, Watts said.
"We need two things. One is $300 million over the next five or six years in terms of contributions from the federal government, over and above what Florida gets now," Watts said.
"We also need to get some help in backing the bonds, guaranteeing the bonds," Watts said. "The state of Florida is just not big enough to do that on our own."
Pena made no promises, but indicated that his department supports the project. That support will be crucial when Florida's request ultimately goes before Congress, Watt said.

"The thing that was key in his reply is the reaction by the federal government that this project is of national significance in bringing high-speed ground transportation to the United States," Watt said. "His indication was that this reallyis important not just in Florida but in other parts of the country."
Watt said it would be premature to guess when the first revenue bonds would be issued for the project or how big the issue would be.
The consortium awarded the bid for the project, Florida Overland eXpress, is made up of Fluor Daniel, Bombardier Inc, GEC Alsthom, and Odebrecht Contractors of Florida, a unit of Odebrecht SA.
